clue.text: Sweetener originally placed in the palm?

definitions.text: Sweetener originally placed in the palm?

parts.words: Sweetener originally placed in the palm?
parts.note: a sweetening product whose fruit first grew on a palm tree, while the surface suggests a sweet put into someone's hand

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a sweet first pressed into their open hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Palm' reads as the hand, but it is the tree whose fruit is dried and ground to make this sweetener.
explanation.definitionFit: This sweetener is made by drying and grinding the fruit of a palm tree.

clue.text: Step from carriage on thoroughfare

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it, so carriage comes after thoroughfare

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a thoroughfare
air means bearing or manner, one's carriage

explanation.surface: Someone steps down from a coach onto the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' suggests a coach, but here it means bearing, as in an air of confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A single tread of a staircase is one step.

clue.text: Florentine count not exactly big up in Oderzo at first

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about, so not exactly
to big up something is to praise it, to laud it

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letters of the words in and Oderzo

explanation.surface: An Italian nobleman is somewhat praised on arrival in the town of Oderzo.
explanation.walkthrough: Claudio is the young Florentine count in Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: In Much Ado About Nothing the character Claudio is a nobleman of Florence holding the rank of count.

clue.text: Hum, when going about work, the end of this?

definitions.text: Hum, when going about work, the end of this?

indicators.note: going about tells us the smell goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a hum is a bad smell, a pong
OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: the end of picks the last letter of the word this

explanation.surface: A tune you hum while busy at work, ending up stuck in your head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hum' looks like the musical sense, but here it is a bad smell, and 'going about' wraps it round the rest. Read whole, the clue describes the tune you hum at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchy chart number is exactly the kind of tune people hum while working.

clue.text: Two girls crash party in Ireland

parts.note: Fi is a short form of the girl's name Fiona
Anna is a girl's name
to crash is to fail, as a business does

explanation.surface: A pair of young women gatecrash a party somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests a celebration, but it is a political party; 'crash' looks like gatecrashing but gives FAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Fianna Fáil is one of the main political parties of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: I don't know a way through

definitions.meaning: saying ... in a quiz means you cannot answer
a mountain ... is a route through high ground

explanation.definitionFit: Pass is what a quiz contestant says when stumped, and it is also a route between mountains.

clue.text: Bowled beamer, mostly to get old captain dismissed

parts.note: B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a beamer is something that beams, a light

explanation.surface: A cricketer bowls a dangerous full toss to get the opposing captain out.
explanation.walkthrough: A beamer in cricket is a ball that reaches the batsman at head height; here it is just a light. William Bligh, captain of the Bounty, was set adrift by mutineers and later deposed as governor of New South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain William Bligh of HMS Bounty was ousted by mutineers and later removed as colonial governor.

clue.text: Brit parent forbidding a certain hairstyle

parts.note: Pom is Australian slang for a British person
pa is an informal word for father, a parent
a forbidding look is a dour, stern one

explanation.surface: A stern British father disapproves of a particular way of wearing hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forbidding' looks like a verb (banning a hairstyle) but is the adjective meaning stern, DOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: The pompadour is a style with the hair swept high off the forehead, named after Madame de Pompadour.

clue.text: Like the novel one couldn't put down?

definitions.text: Like the novel one couldn't put down?

parts.words: Like the novel one couldn't put down?
parts.note: a book too gripping to put down, reread as one that a single author could not put down on paper alone

explanation.surface: A reader describes a thrilling page-turner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couldn't put down' is praise for a gripping book, but here 'put down' means write down: one person alone could not, so two wrote it.
explanation.definitionFit: A book composed jointly by two or more authors is one that no single writer produced alone.

clue.text: Drink like firewater? Take less of that!

indicators.note: take less of the words like firewater, keeping only a run of letters from inside them

explanation.surface: Someone warns a drinker that a strong spirit should be cut down on.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'like' and 'firewater'; 'that' points back to those words.
explanation.definitionFit: Kefir is a fermented milk drink from the Caucasus.

clue.text: Persuaded that mended footwear could be picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: shoes that have been mended may have been soled, given new soles

explanation.surface: Repaired shoes might be collected from the cobbler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' suggests collecting the shoes, but it means heard.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sold on an idea is to be convinced by it, so this means won over.

clue.text: Fallout from turning back fine provender is something shocking

indicators.note: turning back means the words fine, provender and is are read backwards as a run

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
provender is animal fodder, feed
taken as written
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy, a treatment by electric shock

explanation.surface: Something shocking results when fodder is returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning back' turns the run fine, provender, is into SIDEEFF. 'Something shocking' is electric shock treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallout means the unwanted consequences of an action, an unintended by-product.

clue.text: Plug fitting — I hesitate to say this might not be needed

definitions.text: Plug fitting — I hesitate to say this might not be needed

parts.note: to plug a product is to advertise it, and an ad is an advertisement
fitting means suitable, apt
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone tentatively suggests an electrical fitting might be unnecessary.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue describes a plug fitting that would not be needed if the plug suited the socket.
explanation.definitionFit: This device lets a plug fit a socket it was not designed for, and is needless if the plug already fits.

clue.text: Quiet at-home? Mine is something different!

definitions.text: Quiet at-home? Mine is something different!

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
to be at home is to be in
a mine is a dig, an excavation

explanation.surface: Someone contrasts a sedate gathering with their own much livelier one.
explanation.walkthrough: An at-home is a quiet reception in one's house; the clue says the speaker's party is noisier.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is a lively, noisy party, quite unlike a sedate reception at home.

clue.text: As one that's been purged of a deadly sin

indicators.note: purged of means the named letter is removed

parts.note: people who act as one are agreed

explanation.surface: Someone has been cleansed of one of the seven deadly sins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purged' suggests absolution, but it removes A from AGREED.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice, one of the seven deadly sins, is an excessive desire for wealth or food.

clue.text: Increasingly fat old poet eating with son

indicators.note: eating means the poet takes the other pieces inside him

parts.note: Homer is the ancient Greek epic poet
and means with, together with
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: An ancient poet dining with his son is getting fatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat' here is a large sum, as in a fat cheque; handsome likewise means generous.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome can mean large or generous, as in a handsome profit, so the comparative means bigger still.

clue.text: Cup substitute missing kick confronted after upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: to confront is to face, so confronted means faced

explanation.surface: A football team, missing a substitute for the cup tie, struggles after a shock defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cup', 'substitute' and 'kick' suggest football; the definition is coffee with its caffeine kick removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Decaffeinated coffee is a cuppa that lacks the stimulant jolt of caffeine.

clue.text: Hail mat that's transformed plant receptacles

indicators.note: transformed means the letters of hail mat are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doormat damaged by hail is turned into something for holding plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany a thalamus is the receptacle, the part of a flower stalk that bears the floral organs.

clue.text: Litter disturbed and collected in dry mop?

indicators.note: collected in means the jumbled letters are placed inside the word for dry

parts.note: sec is French for dry, used of wine

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of and are jumbled

parts.note: a mop is a shock of hair

explanation.surface: Rubbish was stirred up and gathered into a dry mop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' looks like rubbish, but it is the old carried seat. 'Disturbed' jumbles 'and' to DAN, and 'collected in' puts it inside the word for dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter is a covered seat carried on poles, the same thing as this enclosed chair borne by porters.

clue.text: Chap to be acquitted with the passing of time

indicators.note: with the passing of means the letter for time goes away

parts.note: to be acquitted is to get off

explanation.surface: A man hopes to be cleared as time goes by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing of time' sounds like years going by but removes a T.
explanation.definitionFit: Geoff is a man's name, and in crosswords a chap is any man's name.

clue.text: One making good sort of theatre flier

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre
a flier is a pilot, an airman

explanation.surface: A pilot who also acts in theatre comes good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making good' means mending, not succeeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Making good is repairing damage, the job of a fixer of appliances.

clue.text: Drains trenches

definitions.meaning: to sap is to drain someone's energy
military trenches dug toward an enemy position

explanation.definitionFit: Saps are siege trenches, and to sap is to deplete or exhaust.

clue.text: Short expressive song and dance bears fruit

indicators.note: bears means carries within, so the fuss holds the other piece

parts.note: a song and dance is a fuss, ado

indicators.note: short means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: vocal means expressive, outspoken

explanation.surface: A brief expressive number with dancing yields a crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song and dance' looks like a musical number but means a fuss; 'Short' trims the word for expressive, and 'bears' sets the result inside the fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is the pear-shaped fruit of a tropical tree.

clue.text: Hospital doctor who's done less about containing matter

indicators.note: containing means the reversed word holds the other piece
about means the word is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: meat done less is rarer, so one done less is rarer
the gist is the substance or matter of something

explanation.surface: A doctor who does less work gets round to the issue in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' reverses RARER to RERAR, which then holds GIST.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a registrar is a senior doctor in training, below consultant grade.

clue.text: Be forgetful when preparing fishing equipment? Don't believe it!

definitions.text: Be forgetful when preparing fishing equipment?
definitions.meaning: split as ..., pack zero flies, which is what a forgetful angler does
an exclamation that a story is a complete fabrication

explanation.definitionFit: A tissue of untruths is something not to be believed, and split differently it gives an angler packing zero flies.

clue.text: Endorses Austrian film director's obscure way of communicating

parts.note: to endorse is to back
Fritz Lang was the Austrian-born director of Metropolis

explanation.surface: Someone supports a film-maker's cryptic way of talking.
explanation.walkthrough: Back slang is British street slang that says words backwards, such as 'yob' for boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Back slang is a secret argot formed by saying words backwards, hard for outsiders to follow.

clue.text: Quietly courts one fleeing wealthy tribal head

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
atria are courts, open central halls

indicators.note: fleeing means the letter for one leaves the word

parts.note: wealthy means rich
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone discreetly woos a rich chief, then runs off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courts' looks like wooing but is a plural noun, ATRIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriarch is the male head of a family or tribe.

clue.text: Mural: one depicting Scottish champion

parts.note: mural means relating to a wall, so here it stands for a wall
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A wall painting portrays a Scottish hero.
explanation.walkthrough: William Wallace led the Scots against Edward I.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wallace was a Scottish patriot who led resistance to English rule, a national hero.

clue.text: Work formed source of erotic novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made new by rearranging
source of picks the first letter of erotic

explanation.surface: A piece of writing grew out of a racy novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the book but is the anagram signal; Freedom is a 2010 novel by Jonathan Franzen.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom is the title of a celebrated novel by Jonathan Franzen, a literary work.

clue.text: Read out letters from outskirts of Southern German city

indicators.note: read out means the two letters are spoken as their names, which are then written down
outskirts of picks the first and last letters of the word Southern

explanation.surface: Someone recites letters from the edge of a southern German town.
explanation.walkthrough: The outside letters of 'Southern' are S and N, whose names are written ESS and EN.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr in western Germany.

clue.text: Bank requisitions good for a dynamic economy

indicators.note: requisitions means takes in, so the bank holds the letter for good

parts.note: a bank is a tier, a row or level

explanation.surface: A bank commandeers assets to fuel rapid growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests finance, but it is a row of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger economy is the term for a fast-growing economy, first used of East Asian states.

clue.text: What makes shoe skidproof and sort of stable

definitions.meaning: ... on a boot sole give grip
a farm where horses are kept for breeding

explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a grip spike on a boot sole and also an establishment for breeding horses.
